title: Eastern Cottonwood: Giant Cottonwoods You Can Visit
meta_description: The fast giant of American river bottoms. La Crosse named a marsh trail after its cottonwood, a trunk 7.92 metres round on Wisconsin's champion register.
intro: The eastern cottonwood is the fast giant of North American river bottoms, a poplar that puts on wood quickly in wet ground and seldom lives as long as its size suggests. La Crosse named the Cottonwood Trail after the one in its river marsh, 7.92 metres round and Wisconsin's champion when it was nominated. Ohio's champion at the edge of Alum Creek State Park lost its title to storm damage in 2020, by a local report, and a reader's photograph in the snow shows a trunk splitting into stems as wide as ordinary trees. Two more stand in Cook County's forest preserves near Chicago, 41.5 and 39 metres tall, and neither ranks first in the county. Allentown's, beside the Little Lehigh Creek, has not been reported since somebody ran a tape round it in 2009. If you walk past one, tell us it still stands.
